short_answer: The Machine's Picks is a real, long running business. It names a company, Machines Picks Inc., publishes a full price list and refund terms, and has customer reviews under the same name going back to 2014. Picks go out by text or email, and the site says 2026 results are posted daily on its X page.

Whether its picks make money is much harder to answer. The headline numbers, 10,116-6,134, 62.3% and +22,635 units since 2011, come from the seller's own yearly tables. The site says itself that earlier years are shown as yearly totals, not a pick by pick log. The one detailed log it offers is a three month sample it chose, Q1 2026, with no time each pick was sent.
Treat it as an established seller with an unproven record. If you buy, start short, log every pick with the line you actually got, and judge it after a few hundred picks rather than one streak.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on themachinespicks.com on 7 Nov 2026. All Sports memberships include every official release across active sports for the length you buy. Payment by card, PayPal or Apple Pay, with Venmo, crypto, Afterpay or Klarna offered by request or subject to approval.

guarantee: There is no performance guarantee. The packages page says "All sales are final except where required by applicable law or as expressly provided in our Terms of Service." The terms say members are not entitled to refunds because of losing selections, poor results, dissatisfaction with performance, or not using the membership, and that the company does not guarantee any number of releases in a period.

The terms do promise a remedy for delivery problems. If picks fail to arrive, the company says it will review the case and may restore access, fix delivery, extend access or issue a refund. That covers service failures, not losing bets.

claims_note: The record page says plainly that years before 2026 are shown as yearly totals by sport, not as a public log of individual picks. A buyer cannot check a single pick from 2011 to 2025.

The yearly totals are unusually even: every one of 15 seasons lands between about +1,100 and +1,700 units. Real betting results usually swing much more from year to year. That does not prove anything is wrong, but it is a reason to ask for the picks behind the totals.
A three month sample picked by the seller says little about a full year. The quarter shown, at 67.7%, is well above the seller's own 15 year average.

Testimonials on the site do not all match Trustpilot. The same Brandon Scott quote is dated Feb 2022 on the packages page and Aug 2025 on the proof page (Trustpilot shows Aug 2025), and two 2026 quotes the site attributes to Trustpilot were not among the reviews Trustpilot displayed for the company on 7 Nov 2026.
record: What a buyer can check outside the seller: nothing independent. We found no third party monitor, contest result or regulator record for The Machine's Picks, and the Better Business Bureau search returned no results.

What is the seller's own marketing: the site publishes yearly records by sport for 2011 to 2025, with a downloadable CSV of those yearly totals, and a pick by pick table for 1 Jan to 31 Mar 2026 showing the selection, line, odds, unit rating and result. That table has no time each pick was sent. The homepage shows recent cards, 18-11 and +67.3 units on 7 Nov 2026, and says completed 2026 results will be added after year end. Units are large and uneven: many releases are 5 or 10 units, and one Q1 loss cost 15 units, so a record in wins and losses says little without unit sizes.
We found no court or regulator action involving The Machine's Picks or Machines Picks Inc. in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition The Machine's Picks is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: The Machine's Picks advertises 62.3% over 16,250 picks. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Customer evidence on The Machine's Picks spans 2014 to 2026 but is small: 19 Trustpilot reviews and 14 on CapperTek. Most are positive and describe short runs or single big plays. The seller also quotes some of these reviews on its own site. Below is what we read.

customers.text: Trustpilot showed 19 reviews and a 4.2 score, 79% five star and 11% one star, on an unclaimed profile, with only 4 reviews in the last 12 months.

A CapperTek reviewer said he sees ads for the service constantly on social media, found the price a bit high, and tracked the free picks for about twelve weeks with only one or two wins. He also said he did not remember the older reviews and wondered whether dates could be faked. These are his claims.
A Trustpilot reviewer called the service decent but said the prices are far too expensive.
A Trustpilot reviewer said he had tried about a dozen pick services and that this one is more honest about its record and avoids outrageous claims.
A Trustpilot review marked verified said the win rate had been great, though the number of plays was lower than the reviewer wanted.

A Trustpilot reviewer with eight reviews on the platform said the service is honest with no hidden losses and that the reviewer had just hit a fifth straight "hammer play." The seller quotes this review on its homepage, packages page and proof page.
A one star Trustpilot reviewer called the service a scam, saying it would not offer free picks to monitor and that nobody hits 64%. This is the reviewer's claim.
A one star Trustpilot reviewer said he was told the service wins 70% and that he won 39% after one month.
A CapperTek reviewer said he had emailed for over a week trying to cancel his service without a response.

Most of the 14 CapperTek reviews are positive and describe streaks or big rated plays: 26-4 in 2014, 18 straight winning days in KBO in 2020, a 3 for 3 day pass in 2024, and 56-29 in 2025. A 2014 reviewer noted that picks were sent hours before games and posted on the website after the game started.

The Better Business Bureau search returned no results for Machines Picks, and we found no Reddit, TheRX, SBR or Covers forum thread about this service. Old SBR posts under a "Machine" name appear to be a different handicapper.

conflicts: The site grades its own picks and also sells them. The yearly totals, the Q1 sample and the free play record are all published by the seller.

The "Featured in Publications" logos are presented as coverage, but the Benzinga link points to Benzinga's press release section, which normally carries material a company submits itself rather than independent reporting.
We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the pages we opened.
strengths: A named company, a full price list from a $99 day pass up, and written refund terms.
A pick by pick sample for Q1 2026 with line, odds, units and result, losses included.
Reviews under the same name go back to 2014, so the business has a long public history.
Picks arrive by text or email, with no group chat to join.
concerns: No pick log for 2011 to 2025. The 15 year record is yearly totals only, and the totals are unusually smooth.
No send times in the Q1 sample, and the sample was chosen by the seller.
High prices: $795 a month and $3,995 a year. No refund for losing picks.
Some testimonials on the site carry dates that do not match Trustpilot, or did not appear on Trustpilot today.
Large, uneven unit sizes mean one losing 10 or 15 unit play can erase many small wins.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business, Machines Picks Inc., with published prices, refund terms and customer reviews under the same name since 2014. We could not verify its long term record, because it publishes yearly totals rather than a log of every pick.
How much does The Machine's Picks cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 passes were $99 for a day, $395 a week, $795 a month, $2,895 for six months, $3,995 a year and $5,895 for two years, with season passes from $1,249. All sales are final except where the law or its terms require otherwise.
Does The Machine's Picks have a verified record?

No. The 62.3% and +22,635 unit figures come from the seller's own yearly tables, the only individual picks shown are a seller chosen Q1 2026 sample without send times, and Watchdog has no graded record for it.
Is The Machine's Picks worth it?

For the money you get every official pick across active sports by text or email for the length you buy. What is unproven is whether a buyer, getting the line available at release, beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over time after paying $795 a month or more, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
